title: Excretion Summary
content:
# Excretion Summary

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Review the key concepts of excretion
- Link the roles of the liver and kidneys
- Understand how excretion maintains homeostasis
- Apply knowledge to exam-style questions

## Introduction

This lesson summarises the key concepts of excretion. Excretion is essential for removing metabolic waste products and maintaining a stable internal environment. The liver and kidneys work together to achieve this.

## Key Concepts

### Overview of Excretion

**Definition:** Removal of metabolic waste products from the body

**Not egestion:** Faeces are not metabolic waste

**Main waste products:**
| Waste | Source | Excreted by |
|-------|--------|-------------|
| Carbon dioxide | Respiration | Lungs |
| Urea | Protein breakdown | Kidneys |
| Excess water | Various | Kidneys |
| Excess salts | Diet | Kidneys |

### The Liver's Role

**Key function:** Makes urea from excess amino acids

**Process:**
1. Excess amino acids deaminated
2. Amino group removed → ammonia
3. Ammonia converted to urea (ornithine cycle)
4. Urea released into blood

**Equation:**
$$2NH_3 + CO_2 \rightarrow CO(NH_2)_2 + H_2O$$

**Other functions:**
- Detoxification (alcohol, drugs)
- Bile production
- Glycogen storage
- Plasma protein synthesis

### The Kidney's Role

**Key function:** Filter blood and produce urine

**Processes:**
| Process | What happens | Where |
|---------|--------------|-------|
| Ultrafiltration | Small molecules filtered from blood | Glomerulus |
| Selective reabsorption | Useful substances returned to blood | PCT mainly |
| Secretion | Some substances added to filtrate | DCT |
| Osmoregulation | Water balance controlled | Collecting duct |

### Nephron Summary

| Part | Function |
|------|----------|
| Bowman's capsule | Receives filtrate |
| Glomerulus | Site of ultrafiltration |
| PCT | Main reabsorption site |
| Loop of Henle | Creates concentration gradient |
| DCT | Fine-tuning, hormone control |
| Collecting duct | Water reabsorption (ADH control) |

### Ultrafiltration Summary

| Filtered | Not filtered |
|----------|---------------|
| Water | Blood cells |
| Glucose | Proteins |
| Amino acids | Large molecules |
| Urea | |
| Salts | |

### Selective Reabsorption Summary

| Reabsorbed | How much | How |
|------------|----------|-----|
| Glucose | 100% | Active transport |
| Amino acids | 100% | Active transport |
| Water | ~99% | Osmosis |
| Salts | ~99% | Active/passive |
| Urea | ~50% | Diffusion |

### Water Balance Summary

| Condition | ADH | Collecting duct | Urine |
|-----------|-----|-----------------|-------|
| Dehydrated | High | More permeable | Concentrated, low volume |
| Hydrated | Low | Less permeable | Dilute, high volume |

**Negative feedback:**
1. Change detected by osmoreceptors
2. Hypothalamus responds
3. ADH release adjusted
4. Kidney response corrects change
5. Normal water balance restored

### Linking Liver and Kidneys

| Organ | Produces | Excretes |
|-------|----------|----------|
| Liver | Urea (from amino acids) | - |
| Kidneys | - | Urea (in urine) |

**The connection:**
1. Liver makes urea
2. Urea enters blood
3. Blood goes to kidneys
4. Kidneys filter urea
5. Urea excreted in urine

### Treatment of Kidney Failure

| Treatment | Principle | Advantages | Disadvantages |
|-----------|-----------|------------|---------------|
| Dialysis | Artificial filtering | Available, no surgery | Time-consuming, restrictions |
| Transplant | Replace kidney | Better quality of life | Surgery risk, rejection, shortage |

### Key Equations

**Deamination:**
$$\text{Amino acid} \rightarrow \text{Ammonia} + \text{Keto acid}$$

**Urea formation:**
$$2NH_3 + CO_2 \rightarrow CO(NH_2)_2 + H_2O$$

### Key Diagrams to Know

| Diagram | Key labels |
|---------|------------|
| Kidney cross-section | Cortex, medulla, pelvis, ureter |
| Nephron | Bowman's capsule, glomerulus, PCT, loop of Henle, DCT, collecting duct |
| Ultrafiltration | Afferent/efferent arterioles, filtration barrier |
| ADH action | Pituitary, ADH, collecting duct, aquaporins |

### Links to Other Topics

| Topic | Connection |
|-------|------------|
| Respiration | Produces CO₂ (excreted by lungs) |
| Nutrition | Produces excess amino acids |
| Transport | Blood carries wastes |
| Homeostasis | Maintains stable internal environment |
| Enzymes | Involved in deamination, urea cycle |

### Common Calculations

**Filtration rate:**
$$GFR = \frac{\text{Volume filtered}}{\text{Time}}$$

**Reabsorption:**
$$\%\text{ reabsorbed} = \frac{\text{Filtered} - \text{Excreted}}{\text{Filtered}} \times 100$$

## Common Exam Questions

- Define excretion and give examples
- Describe urea formation in the liver
- Explain ultrafiltration and selective reabsorption
- Describe how ADH controls water balance
- Compare dialysis and transplant

## Common Misconceptions Review

| Misconception | Reality |
|--------------|----------|
| Faeces are excretion | Faeces are egested, not excreted |
| Liver excretes urea | Liver makes urea; kidneys excrete |
| All filtrate becomes urine | ~99% is reabsorbed |
| ADH makes more urine | ADH reduces urine volume |
| Dialysis cures kidney failure | Dialysis manages; doesn't cure |

## Practice Questions

1. Define excretion and name two excretory products. (3 marks)

2. Describe the role of the liver in excretion. (4 marks)

3. Explain how urea is formed from excess amino acids. (3 marks)

4. Compare ultrafiltration and selective reabsorption. (4 marks)

5. Describe how ADH controls water balance. (4 marks)

6. Discuss the importance of excretion in maintaining a stable internal environment. Include the roles of the liver and kidneys, and the consequences of excretory failure. (6 marks)

## Key Terms Review

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Excretion | Removal of metabolic waste products |
| Deamination | Removal of amino group from amino acids |
| Urea | Nitrogenous waste produced from ammonia |
| Ultrafiltration | Pressure-driven filtration in glomerulus |
| Selective reabsorption | Return of useful substances to blood |
| ADH | Hormone controlling water reabsorption |
| Nephron | Functional unit of kidney |
| Dialysis | Artificial blood filtering |

## Summary

- Excretion removes metabolic wastes: CO₂, urea, excess water/salts
- Liver makes urea from excess amino acids (deamination → ornithine cycle)
- Kidneys filter blood (ultrafiltration) and reabsorb useful substances
- ~180 L filtered daily; ~1-2 L urine produced
- ADH controls water reabsorption (negative feedback)
- Kidney failure treated by dialysis or transplant
- Excretion is essential for homeostasis
